title: Baber–Johnson–Talbot triangle-density conjecture for tripartite graphs
statement:
Let $R=\{(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in[0,1]^3:\alpha\beta+\gamma>1,\alpha\gamma+\beta>1,\beta\gamma+\alpha>1\}$, and let

$$
\Delta(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)=\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2-2\alpha\beta-2\alpha\gamma-2\beta\gamma+4\alpha\beta\gamma.
$$

Define $R_1=\{(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in R:\Delta(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\geq 0\}$ and $R_2=R\setminus R_1$. Let $T_{min}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ denote the minimum number of triangles in a tripartite graph with the stated densities, divided by $n^3$. **Baber–Johnson–Talbot conjecture.** If $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in R_2$, then

$$
T_{min}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)=2\sqrt{\alpha\beta(1-\gamma)}+2\gamma-2.
$$

The cited Baber–Johnson–Talbot result gives only the corresponding upper bound in the source, so equality remains unresolved there. The formula would determine the minimum triangle density throughout the region $R_2$.
source_name: Mingyang Guo and Klas Markström, “Density conditions for k vertex-disjoint triangles in tripartite graphs”, arXiv:2503.05218 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.05218

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).
